Done. All 17 tests in `markdown_test.go` pass, and I only modified `markdown.go` (test files untouched, no new files added — my temporary probe directory was removed). ## What I did Per `.docs/instructions.md`, this is a refactoring exercise: the original code worked but was a byte-at-a-time loop tangled with five interacting flags (`header`, `he`, `list`, `listOpened`, `pos`) plus up-front whole-document `strings.Replace` calls for emphasis. The new `markdown.go` is line-oriented, since every supported construct is line-oriented: - **`Render`** splits the input on `\n` and renders each line as exactly one block: - `* ` prefix → list item; consecutive items share one `
    `, and the first non-list line (or end of input) closes it - 1–6 `#` + space → `…` (7+ `#` is not a valid level → literal paragraph text) - anything else → `

    …

    ` - **Small named helpers** replace the flag soup: `isListItem`, `headerLevel`, `renderHeader`, `applyEmphasis`, `replaceFirstPair`, `prefixRunes`. - **Emphasis** is applied per line: first `__pair__` → ``, then first `_pair_` → `` (bold before italic so `__` isn't mistaken for two italics) — same "first pair only" semantics as the original. - A comment block at the top documents the refactoring, as the spec suggested. I first verified the baseline (all tests passed) and probed the original's behavior on untested inputs, which surfaced latent bugs the rewrite also fixes for free: the old code **panicked on a trailing newline** (index out of range) and mangled inputs like `# h\n# h2` (second header rendered as literal `# h2` inside a `

    `). The new code handles those sensibly, while matching the original exactly on everything the tests cover.
